Dear Dr Smiley,

Re: Mrs, Elizabeth Miro, DOB; 23/10/1970

Thank you for seeing Mrs. Miro, a 49-year-old technician who has been diagnosed with

inflammatory breast cancer and requires your urgent assessment

Mrs. Miro has a 2-month history of pain and swelling of the right breast that has not
responded to an antibiotic course. Hef mammogram and ultrasound scan of the breasts show
marked skin thickening of the right breast and a deep irregular mass of 4 mm in diameter
associated with two enlarged ipsilateral axillary lymph nodes. A core-needle biopsy of the

mass confirmed the diagnosis of infiltrating ductal carcinoma

A month ago, Mrs. Miro initially presented with a tender, enlarged and warm right breast
along with palpable axillary nodes. | prescribed the antibiotic course and ordered the
mammogram and the ultrasound scan. However, she defaulted her review and only
Febresented yesterday with when her condition had progressed to include pitted skin and a
retracted nipple. She also complained of recurrent symptoms of her depression, which was
